children: Tropical Storm Edouard formed just off the Texas Coast and is heading towards Port Arthur, Texas, according to the latest forecast from the National Hurricane Center, with the storm expected to reach the coast Tuesday afternoon.

As of the latest 8 a.m. ET NHC update, the storm was showing significant strengthening as it nears landfall along the northwestern Gulf Coast later today, with the center of the storm set to make impact near Port Arthur.

The NHC's latest alert showed a storm surge warning in affect from High Island, Texas, to the Vermilion/Cameron Parish line in Louisiana, with a hurricane  watch in effect from High Island to Cameron, La. Additionally, a larges area of the Gulf Coast saw a tropical storm warning which stretches from Port Bolivar, Texas, to the Vermilion/Iberia Parish line.
The latest outlook showed the storm moving west-northwest around 8 mph, and  is expected to reach the Port Arthur area later Tuesday afternoon and move inland over southeast Texas during the evening.

The storm is current showing sustained winds of 40 mph with high gusts and could significantly strengthening and near hurricane force winds before reaching the coast. NHC said the storm is a small tropical cyclone and tropical storm force winds could extend up to 25 miles from the center of the storm.

The storm is expected to produce rainfalls totaling 3-6 inches with maximum totals up to 9 inches for areas of the upper Texas Coast inland through east-central Texas, according to Tuesday's NHC update. There is also the potential for 2-4 inches of rain in far southwest Louisiana.
NHC will provide another update on the storm's status at 11 a.m. ET.
As of about 10 a.m. ET, market sources were reporting little to no impact on the spot market or refinery operations in the area.
